Bright: English word name, from Old English beorht, 'shining, radiant'; also used as a Nigerian given name.
Einar: Old Norse, from ein 'one, alone' and herjar 'warrior', so 'lone warrior'. Common in Scandinavia.
Ezékiel: French-accented form of Ezekiel, Hebrew Yechezkel, 'God strengthens'.
Gustin: Probably a variant of Gustin or Augustin, from Latin augustus 'venerable'; or a Gustav form. Origin uncertain.
Hashim: Arabic, 'crusher of bread', an ancestor of the Prophet's clan, Banu Hashim.
Juliëtte: Dutch-spelled form of Juliette, French diminutive of Julie, from Latin Julius.
Matiss: Latvian form of Matthias, from Hebrew Mattityahu, 'gift of God'.
Milian: Probably a short form of Emilian or Maximilian, from Latin Aemilianus or Maximilianus. Also a Spanish surname.
Noélya: Modern French coinage from Noël, Latin natalis, 'birth, Christmas', with the ending -ya.
Puk: Dutch, from Puck, a mischievous sprite of English folklore (Old English puca).
Roeya: Probably Arabic ru'ya, 'vision, sight'; spelling varies. Origin partly uncertain.
Rozie: Pet form of Rose, from Germanic hrod 'fame' or Latin rosa 'rose'.
Shems: Arabic shams, 'sun'; also a short form of Shams al-Din.
Slimane: North African French form of Sulayman, Arabic form of Solomon, Hebrew 'peaceful'.
Stavros: Greek, 'cross', often a form of Stavros as a religious name.
Télia: Probably a variant of Thelia or Telia; possibly from Greek telos 'perfect'. Origin uncertain.
Zac: Short form of Zachary, Hebrew Zekharyah, 'the Lord remembers'.
Asal: Arabic, 'honey'; also a Persian and Turkish name.
Evanna: Feminine form of Evan, Welsh, from John, 'God is gracious'; also Irish Éabha 'life'.
Giulya: Probably a variant of Giulia or Julia, Italian form of Julius, Latin Julius, possibly 'youthful'.
Innaya: Probably a variant of Inaya, Arabic, 'care, concern, providence'.
Kajetan: Polish, Czech and German form of Cajetan, Latin Caietanus, 'from Gaeta', an Italian town.
Keila: Probably a variant of Keila or Kayla, possibly Hebrew 'crown' or Irish 'slender'. Origin uncertain.
Khaleesi: Invented in Game of Thrones, the title of a Dothraki queen; coined by George R. R. Martin.
Lucette: French diminutive of Lucie, from Latin lux 'light'.
Mané: Spanish and Portuguese short form of Manuel, Hebrew Immanuel, 'God is with us'; or Senegalese surname.
Nikolay: Russian and Bulgarian form of Nicholas, Greek Nikolaos, 'victory of the people'.
Rex: Latin, 'king'. Used as a given name since the 19th century.
Alis: Variant of Alice or Alys, from Old French Aalis, a short form of Adelheid, 'noble kind'.
Azélya: Probably a variant of Azalea, the flower, Greek azaleos 'dry'.
Ed: Short form of Edward, Old English ead 'wealth, fortune' and weard 'guardian'.
Elenore: Variant of Eleanor, probably from Provençal Aliénor, or from Greek Helen, 'torch'. Origin debated.
Esty: Yiddish short form of Esther, probably from Persian 'star' or Akkadian Ishtar.
Jaylee: Modern American coinage, a blend of Jay and Lee.
Joulia: Greek and Russian form of Julia, from Latin Julius, possibly 'youthful'.
Keïla: Probably a variant of Keila or Kayla; origin uncertain, possibly Hebrew 'crown' or Gaelic 'slender'.
Koby: Short form of Jacob in Hebrew (Kobi), 'holder of the heel'; also English variant of Kobe.
Lily-Roos: Compound of Lily, from the flower, and Dutch Roos, 'rose'.
Louïc: Breton, a variant of Loïc, a Breton form of Louis, Germanic 'famous warrior'.
Nyoh: Origin uncertain; probably a rare or coined name, perhaps a respelling of Noah.
Tahina: Probably Malagasy or Polynesian; Arabic Tahina and Hebrew meanings possible. Origin uncertain.
Yuvraj: Sanskrit and Hindi, 'crown prince', from yuva 'young' and raja 'king'.
Célèste: French form of Celeste, from Latin caelestis, 'heavenly'.
Faylinn: Modern coined name, blending Fay ('fairy, faith') with the suffix -lynn.
Ishaak: Dutch and Arabic form of Isaac, Hebrew Yitzchak, 'he will laugh'.
Kaïla: Probably a variant of Kayla or Keila; possibly Hebrew 'crown' or a coined name. Origin uncertain.
Kyria: Greek, from kyrios 'lord', so 'lady'; the feminine form of Kyrios.
Luìz: Portuguese form of Luís (Louis), Germanic 'famous warrior'; accent variant.
Mazin: Arabic mazin, 'rain clouds' or 'carrier of rain clouds'.
Maélya: Modern French coinage, from Maël (Breton 'prince') with the feminine ending -ya.
Otice: Probably a modern coined name, possibly related to Otis or Otis-derived forms. Origin uncertain.
Tiesj: Limburgish or Flemish spelling of Thijs, short form of Matthijs, Hebrew Matthew, 'gift of God'.
Diago: Variant of Diego or Diogo, Spanish and Portuguese, possibly from Santiago (James), Hebrew 'holder of the heel'.
Elifnur: Turkish, a compound of Elif, the first letter of the Arabic alphabet, and nur, 'light'.
Fahed: Arabic, from fahd, 'lynx, panther'. Variant of Fahd.
Harriet: English feminine form of Harry, Henry, from Germanic heimric 'home ruler'.
Hassatou: West African form of Hasna or Hassana, Arabic, 'beautiful, good'.
Kaylah: Variant of Kayla, possibly from Hebrew kalah 'crown, bride' or Irish 'slender'. Modern coinage.
Milosz: Polish Miłosz, from miłość 'love, grace'. Used by the poet Czesław Miłosz.
Alyce: Variant of Alice, from Old French Aalis, short form of Adelheid, 'noble kind'.
Esmay: Probably a variant of Esmée or Esmae, from Old French esmé, 'esteemed, loved'.
Indie: English, from 'India', or short for 'independent'; also a pet form of Indiana.
Iyas: Arabic Iyas, 'gift, reward', or from iyas 'giving, compensation'.
Kabir: Arabic and Hindi, 'great, powerful'; also a 15th-century Indian poet-saint.
Kumsal: Turkish, 'sandy beach, dune', a girl's name.
Semm: Probably a Dutch short form or variant of Sem, Hebrew Shem, 'name'; or Sem as the biblical son of Noah.
Sondos: Arabic sundus, 'green silk, brocade' mentioned in the Quran.
Stas: Polish and Russian short form of Stanisław or Stanislav, Slavic, 'glorious government'.
Amelio: Italian and Spanish, a masculine form of Amelia or from Latin Aemilius, 'rival'. Possibly from Germanic amal 'work'.
Aymira: Probably a variant of Amira, Arabic, 'princess', or a modern blend. Origin uncertain.
Catalya: Variant of Catalina, Spanish form of Catherine, from Greek katharos 'pure'.
Eiden: Probably a variant of Aiden, Irish Aodhán, 'little fire'; also a Germanic name. Origin uncertain.
Eliyana: Variant of Eliana, Hebrew, 'my God has answered'.
Hilda: Germanic, from hild, 'battle'; the name of English saint Hilda of Whitby.
Hoorain: Arabic and Urdu, from hur al-ayn, 'beautiful maidens of Paradise'.
Jazzlynn: Modern American coinage, blending Jazz (music) with the suffix -lynn.
Keyden: Modern English-style variant of Kayden or Caden, from Irish cadan 'battle', or invented. Origin uncertain.
Lilyana: Variant of Liliana or Lilian, probably from Latin lilium 'lily'.
Maï-Li: Compound name, French style, possibly May plus Li; or Chinese Mei-Li 'beautiful'. Origin uncertain.
Tefania: Variant of Stefania, Italian form of Stephanie, Greek stephanos, 'crown'.
Alexios: Greek form of Alexis, 'defender', from alexein 'to defend'.
Aïko: Japanese, 'beloved child' or 'little love'; depends on kanji.
Danyal: Arabic and Persian form of Daniel, Hebrew, 'God is my judge'.
Harley: English, from a place name meaning 'hare meadow' or 'rocky wood'. Used for girls here.
Jacky: Pet form of Jack or Jacqueline, ultimately Hebrew Jacob, 'holder of the heel'.
Lyor: Hebrew Lior, 'I have light'; or a variant of Liore. Origin partly uncertain.
Martín: Spanish form of Martin, from Latin Martinus, 'of Mars', the god of war.
Phill: Variant of Phil, short for Philip, Greek philippos, 'lover of horses'.
Rox: Short form of Roxanne or Roxy, from Persian roshanak, 'little star' or 'dawn'.
Zalmen: Yiddish form of Solomon, from Hebrew shlomo, 'peaceful'.
Alyona: Russian, a form of Elena (Helen), Greek 'torch, bright one'.
Ennis: Irish, from Inis, 'island'; also a Turkish and English use.
Mohamed-Amir: Compound of Mohamed, Arabic 'praiseworthy', and Amir, Arabic 'prince, commander'.
Nattéo: Modern blend, perhaps Nathan and Matteo; Hebrew 'gift'. Origin uncertain.
Swan: English word name from the bird; also a French form of Swan, from Old English swan, or Scandinavian Svan.
Thilly: Probably a pet form of Mathilde or Thilda, Germanic 'mighty in battle'.
Tyam: Probably a variant of Tiam or Tyam; origin uncertain.
Yllan: Probably a respelling of Ylan or Ilan, Hebrew 'tree'; also Albanian.
Aliyar: Probably Turkish or Persian, from Ali and yar, 'friend, helper of Ali'. Origin partly uncertain.
Alizéa: Modern French name derived from alizé, the trade wind (from Spanish alisios).
Avleen: Probably Punjabi (Sikh) female name, possibly from Sanskrit 'absorbed' (leen); origin uncertain.
Believe: English word name, from the verb 'believe'; a modern virtue name.
Castille: From the Spanish region Castile, Latin castellum 'castle'; a rare girl's name.
Maysaa: Arabic Maysa, 'proud walk, graceful stride'; also the name of a tree.
Mino: Japanese place and given name; also an Italian short form of names ending in -mino. Origin varies.
Natheo: Probably a variant of Matheo or Nathan, ultimately Hebrew 'gift'. Origin uncertain.
Nellia: Probably a variant of Nelia or Nellie, a pet form of Helen or Cornelia. Origin uncertain.
Noh: Arabic form of Noah, Hebrew Noach, 'rest, comfort'.
Nusayba: Arabic, diminutive of nasab or nasiba, perhaps 'little noble'; a Companion of the Prophet.
Stanisaw: Polish Stanisław with a lost letter, Slavic, 'glory of government' or 'become glorious'.
Aarón: Spanish form of Aaron, Hebrew, of uncertain meaning, perhaps 'exalted' or 'mountain'.
Elios: Greek Helios, 'sun'; also a variant of Elio.
Lott: Dutch short form of Charlotte, from Germanic karl 'free man'; also Lotte.
Léno: Probably a modern French variant of Léo or Lenno; Latin leo 'lion'. Origin uncertain.
Ramla: Arabic, 'sand diviner' or a name of Companion's wife; also a city in Israel.
Saidou: West African form of Saïd, Arabic, 'happy, fortunate'.
Sigge: Swedish, short form of Sigurd or Sigfrid, Old Norse, 'victory' and 'peace' or 'guardian'.
Theana: Greek Theano, 'divine' or 'goddess' (thea); a priestess in the Iliad.
Zayi: Probably a variant of Zayd or Zaiy; Arabic 'abundance, growth'. Origin uncertain.
Assyl: Kazakh and Arabic, from asil, 'noble, genuine, pure'.
Aélys: Probably a modern French coinage, from Aélis or Alice, Germanic 'noble kind'. Origin uncertain.
Bangaly: West African (Guinean, Malinke) male name; origin uncertain.
Elenora: Variant of Eleonora or Eleanor, Italian and Slavic form, possibly from Greek Helen.
Filippos: Greek form of Philip, 'lover of horses'.
Leyah: Variant of Leah, Hebrew, possibly 'weary' or 'wild cow'.
Lijana: Slavic form of Liliana, or a Baltic name; from Latin lilium 'lily'.
Marcelo: Spanish and Portuguese form of Marcellus, Latin, diminutive of Marcus, 'of Mars'.
Mayane: Probably a modern variant of Maya or Mayan, possibly Sanskrit maya 'illusion'. Origin uncertain.
Milane: Probably a respelling of Milan, Slavic mil 'dear, gracious', or the Italian city.
Neymar: Brazilian, popularised by footballer Neymar; derived from his father's name Neymar, origin uncertain.
Valerian: Latin Valerianus, from the family name Valerius, from valere 'to be strong'.
Abbie: English pet form of Abigail, Hebrew, 'my father is joy'.
Edie: English pet form of Edith, Old English ead 'wealth' and gyth 'war'.
Elyzio: Probably from Elysium, Greek paradise, or a form of Elísio, Portuguese; origin uncertain.
Irha: Probably Urdu or Arabic-influenced; origin uncertain.
Ishaac: Variant of Isaac, Hebrew Yitzchak, 'he will laugh'.
Jaline: Probably a modern coinage, blending Jay with -line; origin uncertain.
Mannat: Punjabi and Hindi, 'vow, wish made to God'.
Mollie: English variant of Molly, a pet form of Mary, Hebrew 'beloved' or 'bitter'.
Méllina: Probably a variant of Melina or Mellina, from Greek meli 'honey' or Latin. Origin uncertain.
Negan: Hebrew-style name, popularised by The Walking Dead villain; also Persian 'jewel'. Origin uncertain.
Nellis: Probably from the English surname Nellis, or a variant of Nelis, short form of Cornelis. Origin uncertain.
Ninho: Portuguese, 'nest'; a nickname used by the French rapper Ninho. Origin uncertain as a first name.
Miette: French, 'crumb', also a pet name. Rare as a given name.
Edris: Variant of Idris, Arabic, a prophet mentioned in the Quran, possibly 'interpreter'; or Welsh Edris, 'ardent lord'.
Ieremia: Romanian and Greek-style form of Jeremiah, Hebrew, 'God will raise up'.
Iloan: Probably a Breton-style variant of Iolan or Ilan, Hebrew 'tree'. Origin uncertain.
Nyra: Probably a modern coinage; also Kurdish and Indian 'bright'. Origin uncertain.
Yousaf: Arabic and Urdu form of Yusuf (Joseph), Hebrew, 'God will add'.
Yared: Hebrew and Ethiopian, 'descend' or 'descendant'; Yared was an Ethiopian saint-composer and a biblical patriarch.
Élouan: French form of Elouan, Breton, from Elouan Lou, a saint; possibly 'elk' or 'noble'. Origin uncertain.
Andrra: Probably a variant of Andra or Andrea, Greek andreia, 'manly, brave'. Origin uncertain.
Anna-Belle: Compound of Anna, Hebrew 'grace', and Belle, French 'beautiful'.
Djay: Spelled form of the initials DJ, or a variant of Jay; modern coined name.
Ella-Mae: Compound of Ella, from Germanic 'all, other' or Eleanor, and Mae, a form of May or Mary.
Maeson: Modern variant of Mason, English occupational surname, 'stone worker'.
Menesa: Probably a modern coined name; Arabic 'Minnesa' or Amharic possible. Origin uncertain.
Nerio: Italian, from Latin Nerius, possibly 'strong' or Sabine nero 'strong'; also a Spanish variant.
Lisèle: Probably a French blend of Lise and Elle, a variant of Liselle. Origin uncertain.
Muadh: Arabic Mu'adh, 'protected, sheltered'; a Companion of the Prophet.
Shahan: Persian, 'kings', plural of shah; also Armenian Shahan.
Sofia-Maria: Compound of Sofia, Greek 'wisdom', and Maria, Hebrew Miriam, 'beloved' or 'bitter'.
Eithan: Variant of Ethan, Hebrew, 'strong, firm, enduring'.
Cirilla: Feminine of Cyril, Greek kyrios 'lord'; also known from The Witcher's Princess Cirilla.
Malyah: Modern coined name, possibly from Maliyah or Maya; origin uncertain.
lise: Missing accent: probably Élise, French form of Elisabeth, Hebrew Elisheva, 'my God is an oath'.
Aizah: Arabic and Urdu, 'compensation', or a variant of Aiza, 'honour'.
Lou-Elle: Compound of Lou, from Louise, Germanic 'famous warrior', and Elle.
Maïley: Modern French coinage, possibly a blend of Maï or May and -ley. Origin uncertain.
lonore: Missing accent: probably Éléonore or Aliénor, French form of Eleanor, possibly from Provençal Aliénor.
tefan: Missing character: probably Štefan, Stefan, Slavic form of Stephen, from Greek stephanos 'crown'.
